addresses: blocker (desktop): the reviewer's guard is on the wrong action — 'Approve and add' fires on the first click with nothing on the card saying what it writes, where, or that it cannot be taken back
blocker (phone): seven CSS pixels separate the irreversible button from the recoverable one, and the guard is on the recoverable one
changes.change: Rebuilt the card foot as one geometry used by both of its states. The irreversible action is the filled button; directly beneath it a line names the destination and the finality, per card, with the actual names it will write ('Adds Ethan and Ishaan to Planning Center. Nothing added there can be taken back.'); beneath that line sits the second control. On touch both buttons are 48px and full width, separated by the ~50px the caption occupies; at lg the primary shrinks to content width on the left and the second control is pushed to the card's right edge. Added the missing confirm step, rendered in the armed state on one card: same three slots, primary reads 'Yes — add 3 children', the caption goes warn and names the children and the no-undo, and 'Not ours' steps out for 'Cancel'.
changes.rationale: Two halves, because the finding has two halves. The confirm alone would not help a reviewer who never reads the subhead, so the destination and the finality are in the resting state on every card; the caption alone would still let one press be final, so the confirm exists. Keeping the armed state in the same three slots as the resting one means the thumb never relearns which rectangle is which, and it is what buys the separation on touch without a hard-coded gap. The discard confirm stays — removing a guard to fix an asymmetry is a regression; the asymmetry is corrected upward.
changes.breakpoint: both; the stack-vs-row split is below lg / at lg and up
changes.implementation:
src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx, RegistrationCard. Add `confirmingApprove` beside `confirmingDiscard`. Replace the flex-wrap foot with a column that becomes a row at lg: primary Button (min-h-12 w-full lg:w-auto), caption

(warn when armed, ink-400 otherwise), then the ghost second Button. First press of the primary arms; second calls onApprove. Caption names the children still held (row.children.filter(c => c.pendingReview && !c.mergedIntoStudentId)) rather than counting them.

addresses: blocker (desktop): the merge does not read as something you can press, and the fact that would settle it is hidden behind pressing it
blocker (phone): a 16px-tall target 26px above the irreversible button, styled only with hover:underline, which touch never fires
design major: the one interactive object in the card with no affordance whatsoever
design minor (phone): the merge line inherits centre alignment and orphans 'roster' on its own line
changes.change: Deleted the door. The picker is always open when a child has candidates: a warn one-liner stating the collision, a quiet line stating the asymmetry ('Merging can be undone. A duplicate in Planning Center cannot.'), then the candidates as seated buttons — bg-ink-900, ring-ink-700, text-left, 48px on touch / 36px on a pointer — and a same-shaped ghost 'None of them — Ethan is new'. Chrome is ink, not warn, so they do not read as another notice strip.
changes.rationale: Making it unconditional is less mechanism, not more: it deletes the `picking` state, deletes the invisible control, and makes phone and laptop the same component. It also puts the comparison — the candidate names and their grades — in front of the reviewer at the moment they are about to create a third row. The grade is what tells two Jacob Smiths apart, and it was behind a click.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx, ChildRow. Remove the `picking` state and the collapsed button branch; render the picker whenever candidates.length > 0 && child.studentId. Candidate buttons keep summaryLabel() verbatim, restyled to min-h-12 … ring-1 ring-ink-700 pointer-fine:min-h-9. 'None of them' becomes the same shape and needs a real handler — it should mark the child reviewed-and-new rather than closing a panel that no longer exists.

addresses: visual major: two of five families are decidable above the fold; two columns would put all five inside roughly one fold
design major: the card stretches to the full content column but nothing inside it was composed for that width
changes.change: lg:grid lg:grid-cols-2 lg:items-start on the page frame, header spanning both columns, intro bounded to max-w-2xl. Cards are 568px: the sibling paragraph and both coloured strips wrap to 2–3 lines instead of running the full band, and the Added/Merged badges sit ~330px from their names instead of ~900px. Page height 1931px → 1629px carrying strictly more content.
changes.rationale: One class change answers the density finding and most of the composition finding at once, and it is the layout primitive Insights and Events already use. The empty right column below the last card is left alone: fixing it means re-ordering the queue away from its priority sort or introducing CSS columns as a new mechanism.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx: PageFrame gains lg:grid lg:grid-cols-2 lg:items-start; wrap the header in lg:col-span-2; max-w-2xl on the intro. PageFrame already supplies gap-4, which becomes the grid gap.

addresses: visual major (desktop): the heading carries no count, and the signal separating 'needs a judgement' from 'needs a yes' takes five forms at five depths inside the cards
visual major (phone): no count, so a reviewer with three minutes spends all three on the two least urgent families
changes.change: Count pill in the h1 ('Families to review · 5'), reusing the pill the card headers already use for child counts. And a state badge in CardHeader's existing — previously empty — action slot on the three cards that need a judgement: warn '4 days left', warn 'Possible duplicate', danger 'Push failed'. The two routine cards carry nothing, so the queue reads two-of-five-are-a-yes from the outside edge.
changes.rationale: The Badge component, its tones and the header's action slot all already exist; this is furniture moved, not invented. Colouring only the cards that need thought means the absence of a badge is itself the signal.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx: pass action={…} to CardHeader — Badge tone=warn for the day count when expiringSoon, tone=danger 'Push failed' when row.lastError, tone=warn 'Possible duplicate' when any child has unresolved possibleDuplicates. Heading count is rows.length.

addresses: visual major: the 26-day-old family sits 923px below the fold behind four families that can wait, and its deadline is a phrase rather than a number
changes.change: Queue re-sorted: expiring-soon first, then newest-first. The 26-day-old family moves from card 5 to card 1 — y=1990 to y=345 on the phone. The strip carries the number and what it costs: 'Clears in 4 days and takes the phone number with it. The children stay on Tally's roster with nobody attached to them.' The intro says 'Soonest to be swept first' so the order is legible.
changes.rationale: The one card where doing nothing is itself irreversible should be the one you meet first, and on a device that fits one family per screen the order is the triage. Only the expiry class is hoisted; the rest keeps its newest-first order.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx: sort rows before mapping — expiring-soon first, then registeredAt descending. Strip copy takes Math.ceil(row.expiresInMs / DAY).

addresses: visual major: nothing on this frame or on the core team's home screen tells anyone the queue exists; 72% of the sidebar column is blank
changes.change: A fifth item in the pointer-only sidebar — Review with a neutral count pill — in the same shape as the other four. hidden lg:flex by inheritance from the aside, so the phone tab bar keeps its four door tasks untouched.
changes.rationale: The thumb bar is reserved for the door. A neutral count rather than a warn one: five waiting is not itself an alarm, and the urgency now lives on the first card where it is specific.
changes.implementation: Belongs in the shell's nav list, not in ReviewPage — the aside that renders Check in / Insights / Events / Students. One entry, gated on the same role check that gates /review, with a count. Only the two review prototypes were edited, so the other twelve frozen pages do not show it; the implementation adds it once, in the shell, for all of them.

addresses: design major: the danger strip's text sits a rung lighter than warn, so it reads as neutral and the severity ranking is inverted
changes.change: text-danger-300 → text-danger-400, and both strips from text-xs to text-sm. Also rounded-lg → rounded-xl so they share a radius with the child rows beside them.
changes.rationale: This was a live bug, not only a judgement call: --color-danger-300 is not in the theme, so Tailwind emitted no rule and the strip inherited the card's near-white ink — exactly the 'reads as neutral' the critic saw. danger-400 is the rung warn-400 already sits on, so hue is now the only difference between the two strips.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx: the lastError paragraph becomes rounded-xl … text-sm text-danger-400; the expiringSoon paragraph becomes rounded-xl … text-sm text-warn-400. Confirmed against src/index.css: danger has 400/500/600 only, and this file is the token's only use in the app.

addresses: design minor: the card body has no top padding, so the header's rule is glued to the body and collides with the coloured strips' corners
design minor: four of five cards title themselves with the guardian's name and restate it verbatim one row down
design minor: the allergy is joined to the grade by a middle dot in the card's quietest token
changes.change: Card body gains pt-4 so the rule closes the header and the strips stop running into it. The definition list drops the 'Brought by' row and carries only the phone, removing the repetition and the label column that misaligned the values to a fourth left edge. The allergy breaks onto its own line at text-ink-300, a step up from the grade's text-ink-500, with no new accent.
changes.rationale: All three are one-line edits, all three obviously right, and the dl change removes 20px per card that the two-column layout can spend better.
changes.implementation: src/features/review/ReviewPage.tsx: body div px-4 pt-4 pb-4; the dl becomes a single Phone row; in ChildRow, split gradeSentence(child) and child.allergies into two block spans, the allergy at mt-0.5 text-xs text-ink-300.

declined.finding: design major: the badge should travel with the name it labels instead of with the row's right edge
declined.why: Addressed by width rather than restructure: at 568px the gap is ~330px, not ~900px. Moving the badge inline would break the fixed right-hand badge lane the roster and students rows use — a cross-scene pattern change to close a gap the column width already closed most of.

declined.finding: design minor: the card title needs to step further away from the child names
declined.why: The title is CardHeader, shared by Insights, Events and Students. Changing its type scale to fix one scene's internal hierarchy would move four other screens on a minor finding. The dl change removed the third near-identical treatment of the guardian's name, which was the larger half.

declined.finding: the phone page is now 3324px, up from 2348px
declined.why: The growth is the always-open merge picker and the vertical foot — the two things the blockers asked for. Both phone complaints were about order and count, not length, and both are answered: the expiring family moved from y=1990 to y=345 and the heading carries the count. Flagged so the next round judges it deliberately rather than as a surprise.

declined.finding: a seed artifact, not a design finding: the expiring family's second child carries a duplicate hint pointing at an unrelated roster row, so the candidate reads as a different name than the collision claims
declined.why: Invisible while the candidates were behind a click; visible now that the picker is always open. Fix belongs in e2e/support/triageQueue.ts, not in the prototype.
